name: Chlorine
occurrence: Never free in nature; abundant combined as rock salt and dissolved chloride ions in seawater.
majorUses: Water disinfection and swimming pool sanitation
Bleaching agent in paper and textile industries
biologicalRelevance: As chloride ion, it's essential for stomach acid (HCl) production and fluid/electrolyte balance across cell membranes.
notableCharacteristics: A pale yellow-green toxic gas that was used as a chemical weapon in World War I, yet in dilute controlled form it's what keeps drinking water safe from pathogens.
whyHere: Seven valence electrons put it one short of a stable octet, so it reacts eagerly to gain that electron — powerful enough as an oxidizer to disinfect water, but also toxic enough to have been weaponized historically.
didYouKnow: Chlorine gas is roughly 2.5 times denser than air, which is why it hugs the ground in a leak — a fact both WWI trench soldiers and modern chemical-safety protocols had to reckon with.
genZNote: Useful disinfectant, terrifyingly reactive in the wrong context. Context is doing a lot of work there.
